topic: Berardino: Andersen's fees, and a correction
claim: Berardino's written statement put Andersen's fees from Enron at $52 million. In his spoken statement he said $59 million, including $25 million for the audit and $13 million for consulting; the next day, in a December 13, 2001 letter printed in the record, he asked that the record reflect $52 million 'as the written testimony attests'.
quote: please let the record reflect that Andersen received $52 million from Enron last year as the written testimony attests, rather than the $59 million referred to in oral testimony.

topic: Berardino: January 2002 letter correcting his Chewco testimony
claim: In a January 21, 2002 letter to Chairman Oxley, printed in the hearing record, Berardino wrote that elements of his written and oral testimony about Chewco had been 'unintentionally imprecise'. He said Andersen had not been told in 1997 of a December 30, 1997 agreement under which JEDI put $6 million into a reserve account for Barclays' benefit, so only about half of Chewco's required 3% equity was really at risk; at the hearing he had described this as an agreement between Enron and the bank.
quote: As a result, elements of my written and oral testimony were unintentionally imprecise in some respects.

topic: SEC Chief Accountant on the 3% rule
claim: Testifying at the same hearing, SEC Chief Accountant Robert Herdman explained that under the accounting rules an SPE must have outside common equity of at least 3 percent of its total capital, owned by independent third parties, or else the sponsoring company must consolidate it (put it on its own balance sheet).
quote: It has to be consolidated if the SPE doesn’t have at least 3 percent of its total capital owned by outsiders.

locator.section: Questioning of Robert K. Herdman by Rep. Toomey

notes: line numbers refer to work/text/hrg-hfs-enron-investors-pt1.txt. A contemporary official explanation of the 3% test, good for the glossary entry on the 3% rule / SPE consolidation. Herdman's title from the witness list (p. V): 'Chief Accountant, U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission'. Not sworn per the transcript; 'told the subcommittees' is safest.
